key_insight: Wall curvature reorganizes supersonic turbulence: concave walls promote structured triadic transfers and vortex breakdown, while convex walls suppress redistribution and retain energy in elongated streamwise streaks.
engineering_relevance: Separating nonlinear scale selection from linear flow receptivity can inform modeling and control of supersonic boundary layers over curved aerodynamic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations of concave and convex supersonic boundary layers.
Scale-resolved TKE budgets, transfer bispectra, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition.
Global resolvent analysis to identify linear amplification mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Simulation-based diagnostics identify a concave-wall outer-layer production peak and multi-step triadic transfers, versus suppressed pressure-strain redistribution and localized downstream amplification over convex walls.
watch_item: The abstract provides no parameter ranges or experimental validation, leaving applicability across Mach numbers, Reynolds numbers, and curvature strengths uncertain.
paper_title: Triadic energy cascades and linear amplification mechanisms in supersonic turbulent boundary layers over curved walls
